metadata.workstream: W-01 · Replace city and county proxies with trade-area figures
metadata.subjectGeography: Central Los Angeles (Exact Parcel / APN / Street Address Redacted — Internal Workspace Only)

indicators.indicator: Total Population — Latest State Official Estimate (Jan 1, 2026)
indicators.impact: CA DOF attributes LA County's 2025–2026 loss to Palisades/Eaton wildfire displacement, Inland Empire out-migration, and deportations. Contracting macro population caps organic QSR traffic growth unless local infill densifies the trade area.
indicators.sourceLabel: CA Dept. of Finance E-1 Report (May 2026)

indicators.indicator: Total Population — U.S. Census Bureau Estimates (V2025 / V2024 vs. 2020 Census)
indicators.impact: Irregularity flagged: Census V2025 county estimate is 142K lower than CA DOF Jan 2026 estimate due to differing methodologies; both confirm net contraction since 2020.
City of LA density is 3.4x the county average; high urban density underpins land scarcity for Central LA commercial corridors, though parcel-level tract density must be verified offline.
City of LA median income trails California by 17.3% while housing costs remain elevated — pressuring discretionary dining-out budgets among lower- and middle-income households.

indicators.indicator: Per Capita Income & Poverty Rate (2020–2024 ACS)
indicators.impact: Elevated city poverty rate (16.5%) increases price sensitivity for value-oriented QSR chains following menu price hikes.

indicators.indicator: Owner-Occupancy, Median Home Value & Households (2020–2024 / 2018–2022 ACS)
indicators.impact: Nearly two-thirds of LA City households are renters, creating rent-cost pressure on consumer spending while sustaining long-term multifamily redevelopment demand on transit corridors.

indicators.indicator: MSA Nonfarm Payroll Employment (Sep 2026 Preliminary, NSA)
indicators.countyLA: LA-Long Beach-Anaheim MSA: 6,282,100 (+30,200 / +0.5% YoY; not stat. significant)
indicators.cityLA: City-level workplace mix spans Healthcare, Retail, Professional Services & Hospitality
indicators.impact: Regional payroll growth slowed to +0.5% YoY (statistically unchanged at 90% CI per BLS). Prior sector data (Jun 2025 YoY) showed gains led by Education & Health (+5.5%) while Manufacturing (-3.8%), Financial Activities (-2.3%), Construction (-1.9%), and Prof/Bus Services (-0.6%) declined.

indicators.indicator: MSA Unemployment Rate (Sep 2026 Preliminary & 2021–2025 Annual Averages)
indicators.cityLA: LA City LWDA: 5.6% (May 2025) / 6.0% (Jan 2025) per CA EDD
indicators.impact: Headline MSA unemployment fell to 4.4% in Sep 2026, though civilian labor force declined -1.8% YoY (from 6.769M to 6.647M).
indicators.sourceLabel: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Monthly Metro Release (Oct 2026)

indicators.countyLA: Index 360.965 (Oct 2026, +0.6% MoM); Sep 2026 12-mo change: +3.7% (Oct 12-mo blank in BLS)
indicators.cityLA: US Food Away From Home CPI-U: +3.5% YoY (May 2026) / +3.8% YoY (Mar 2026)
indicators.impact: Persistent ~3.5%–3.7% local inflation erodes flat or low-bump NNN leases while favoring uncapped CPI escalations. Flagged: BLS table shows '-' for Oct 2026 12-mo YoY.

indicators.indicator: California Fast Food Minimum Wage (AB 1228) & LA City General Minimum Wage
indicators.countyLA: CA Fast Food (AB 1228): $20.00/hr (eff. Apr 1, 2024); CA General: $16.90/hr (Jan 1, 2026)
indicators.cityLA: City of LA General Minimum Wage: $18.42/hr (eff. Jul 1, 2026, CPI-W indexed)
indicators.impact: AB 1228 directly applies to Jack in the Box corporate and franchisee units (national chain ≥60 stores), structurally increasing store labor costs and pressuring franchisee margins and rent coverage.
indicators.sourceLabel: CA DIR AB 1228 FAQ & LA Office of Wage Standards (2026)

indicators.indicator: LAUSD Enrollment, Graduation Rate & 10-Yr County K-12 Forecast
indicators.countyLA: CA DOF 2026 Series projects LA County public K-12 enrollment to fall -240,800 over 10 years
indicators.cityLA: LAUSD 2025–26 Enrollment: 497,105 (16.4% EL); 2024–25 Grad Rate: 86.5%; 2024–25 CAASPP record gains (+3.4 ELA, +3.9 Math, +3.3 Sci)
indicators.impact: Improved LAUSD academic results are constructive, but the projected -240,800 countywide K-12 student drop indicates aging/fewer families with children — a headwind for family-driven QSR traffic.
indicators.sourceLabel: CA Dept. of Education (2025–26) & CA DOF K-12 Projections

indicators.indicator: LA Metro D Line (Purple) Subway Extension & SCAG Long-Range Jobs Forecast
indicators.countyLA: SCAG Connect SoCal 2024 projects LA County jobs 5,031,000 (2019) -> 5,461,000 (2050)
indicators.cityLA: D Line Sec. 1 (Wilshire/La Brea, Fairfax, La Cienega) OPENED May 8, 2026; Sec. 2 (Beverly Hills/Century City) & Sec. 3 (Westwood/UCLA 2028 Olympic Village) forecast 2027
indicators.impact: Major Central LA/Mid-Wilshire heavy-rail investment supports long-run transit-oriented land values, though exact parcel proximity to Metro stations must be checked offline.
indicators.sourceLabel: LA Metro D Line Project Page (2026) & SCAG Connect SoCal 2024

indicators.indicator: LA City Community Plans, TOC Incentives & CA AB 2011 Commercial-to-Housing Law
indicators.countyLA: CA AB 2011 enables ministerial multifamily housing along commercial corridors (30–40 du/ac for ≥1-acre sites on corridors <100 ft wide, subject to labor/affordability & relocation rules)
indicators.cityLA: Downtown Community Plan (DTLA 2040) approved May 3, 2023 / revised Dec 4, 2024; Measure JJJ TOC Tiers 1–4 grant 35%+ density bonus within 0.5 mi of major transit
indicators.impact: Redevelopment optionality can establish a strong underlying land value floor if Jack in the Box vacates in 2030–2035 — ONLY after exact zoning, lot size, and TOC/AB 2011 eligibility are verified privately in ZIMAS.
indicators.sourceLabel: LA City Planning & CA Legislature AB 2011

indicators.indicator: Parcel Arterial AADT, Ingress/Egress, Drive-Thru Stacking & Signage
indicators.countyLA: Central LA freeway corridors carry ~231,000–328,000 AADT in LA Planning / Caltrans EIR datasets
indicators.cityLA: LADOT ambient Central City traffic growth factor: 1.0%/yr in Central City North planning EIR
indicators.impact: UNVERIFIED PARCEL INPUT: Must verify exact arterial AADT, corner signalization, drive-thru stacking capacity, and grandfathered drive-thru zoning privately.
indicators.sourceLabel: LA City Planning EIR & Caltrans Traffic Census

indicators.indicator: 1-Mile / 3-Mile / 5-Mile Census Tracts, Daytime Workers & Competing Drive-Thrus
indicators.countyLA: LA County: 304,988 employer establishments; 3,987,736 CBP employment (2023)
indicators.cityLA: City of LA: $17.37B Accommodation & Food Services sales; $81.35B retail sales (2022 Economic Census)
indicators.impact: UNVERIFIED PARCEL INPUT: Must execute offline Census tract selection (2015–19 vs. 2020–24 trends) and local QSR drive-thru competitor / cannibalization audit.
indicators.sourceLabel: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts (2022 Economic Census / 2023 CBP)

projectionFramework.metric: Official Agency Macro Baseline & Capital Markets
projectionFramework.baseProjection: CA DOF shows LA County -0.6% YoY & LA City -0.9% YoY population as of Jan 2026; BLS Sep 2026 MSA jobs +0.5% YoY; CA EDD projects +8.8% statewide job growth 2023–2033 led by Education & Health and Leisure/Hospitality; BLS Sep 2026 LA CPI-U +3.7% YoY; U.S. 10-Yr Treasury 4.91% (11/24/2026).
projectionFramework.upsideCase: Full D Line opening (Sections 2 & 3 forecast 2027) + 2028 Los Angeles Olympics visitor/infrastructure surge + lower Treasury yields + JACK brand stabilization strengthen buyer liquidity.
projectionFramework.downsideCase: Macro downturn lifts LA unemployment while AB 1228 ($20/hr) + persistent inflation compress franchisee margins, elevating 'JACK on Track' store-closure risk ahead of 2030.
projectionFramework.sourceLabel: CA EDD 2025 Jobs Report, CA DOF, BLS, LA Metro, U.S. Treasury

projectionFramework.metric: Structural Demographic, Debt Maturity & Land Value Trajectory
projectionFramework.baseProjection: CA DOF projects slowing state growth (0.13%/yr avg) and -240,800 LA County public K-12 enrollment over 10 yrs; SCAG Connect SoCal 2024 projects gradual LA County employment expansion to 5.461M by 2050; JACK's Series 2026-1 ($500M, ARD May 2031) and Series 2022-1 A-2-II ($503M, ARD Feb 2032) debt maturities land inside this exact lease rollover window.
projectionFramework.upsideCase: Transit-corridor zoning (TOC Tiers 1–4 / AB 2011 / DTLA 2040) establishes an urban infill land floor supporting redevelopment sale or high-credit replacement QSR lease.
projectionFramework.downsideCase: Simultaneous arrival of lease expiry, JACK 2031–2032 securitized debt refinancing, California property insurance inflation, and shrinking family demographics creates severe re-leasing or valuation risk.
projectionFramework.sourceLabel: CA DOF K-12 Projections, SCAG Connect SoCal 2024, SEC Q3 FY26 10-Q
